title: Selected Melkite, Roman Greek and Italo-Greek Eucharistic book states; unresolved local reception

traditions.label: Melkite Greek Catholic liturgy books
traditions.scope: The Melkite patriarchal and synodal Book of the Divine Liturgy, issued in two complementary parts.
traditions.coverage_note: The official retrospective identifies approval and a book; the original Arabic volumes and predecessor texts have not been collated.

traditions.label: Roman Greek celebrant books
traditions.scope: The Holy See approved Greek Hieratikon bearing a 1950 title date and a March 1952 printing colophon.
traditions.coverage_note: A Roman Greek approved edition is attested. Neither printing at the Melkite Paulist press nor Greek language proves adoption by the Melkite Church, the Greek exarchates or Piana degli Albanesi.

traditions.label: Italo-Greek Basilian use of Grottaferrata
traditions.scope: The 1601 Roman printing whose own title names the Italo-Greek Basilian monks and the Grottaferrata Typikon.
traditions.coverage_note: The historical monastic use is distinguished from later use in the Italo-Albanian eparchies of Lungro and Piana.

traditions.label: Hungarian Greek Catholic local book reception
traditions.scope: Hungarian territory and the historical Church Slavonic book witnesses held there.
traditions.coverage_note: A 1646 Lviv printing has later local collection provenance, but no inspected record yet makes it a Hungarian Catholic liturgical-use state.

traditions.label: Bulgarian Greek Catholic local book reception
traditions.scope: Bulgarian service-book publication and possible reception of the Roman Slavonic Vulgata.
traditions.coverage_note: Official local publication lists do not identify a source edition or verify receipt of the Vulgata.

traditions.label: Russian Greek Catholic local book reception
traditions.scope: Russian Catholic holdings of Roman Slavonic books, separate from the Vulgata textual states already in the Byzantine dossier.
traditions.coverage_note: A parish library list establishes possession of copies, not dated celebration with a specified edition.

sources.title: Patriarch Gregorios III, Letter on the Liturgy, patriarchal website
sources.inspection: Foreword 3 and chapter 4, paragraphs 1–5, read on the patriarchal website. The page header reads 18 January 2010; the letter's own closing dateline is 7 March 2011. Chapter 4 reports definitive synodal agreement in 2001 and the appearance of the book in 2006, and directs use of the approved Liturgy books.
sources.limitations: An English presentation of the patriarchal letter; the Arabic book and underlying synodal acts were not acquired or collated. Its 2005–2008 range for the two parts is broad.

sources.title: German Liturgical Institute library, record 47966, Kitab al-Liturgiyat al-ilahiyah al muqaddasah
sources.inspection: Record 47966 read: Patriarchal Liturgical Commission; Jounieh, Paulist press; part 1, Chrysostom, 2006, [8] + 907 pages; part 2, Basil and Presanctified, 2007, [8] + 367 pages.
sources.limitations: The catalogue explicitly offers no digitized copy. Its language codes are not used to infer the language of every page; title and approval leaves remain uninspected.

sources.title: Ἱερατικόν, Rome 1950, Internet Archive copy
sources.inspection: Existing Eastern inventory records direct inspection of original title at PDF p. 3, Holy See approval at p. 4 and colophon at p. 343. This round rechecked the source record, not the 82 MB scan; the Archive landing page did not render through the web reader.
sources.limitations: No exact Greek exarchate, Italo-Albanian or Melkite reception is established. The title year 1950 and the March 1952 end of printing have different date roles; rights for modern editorial text are unresolved.

sources.title: Sacrae liturgiae, Rome 1601, photographed title leaves and antiquarian description
sources.inspection: The original Latin title transcribed on the page names the Chrysostom, Basil and Presanctified liturgies, the Italo-Greek Basilian monks, the Typikon of Grottaferrata, and Aloysius Zannettus at Rome in 1601. The page identifies a second Greek title leaf and a 52-leaf quarto copy.
sources.limitations: Only title photographs and an object description, not a whole-book scan. The stated audience does not document a particular monastery copy's use or later Lungro/Piana adoption.

sources.title: Szent Atanáz Greek Catholic college old-books catalogue, Lviv 1646 Sluzhebnik
sources.inspection: Existing inventory identifies the incomplete Nyírderzs copy and its later college transfer, with a separate reported 1666 donation note whose named church is unresolved. The PDF catalogue was located online this round; original title and ownership leaves were not reexamined.
sources.limitations: Local possession does not establish liturgical use, Catholic approval, or a Hungarian recension.

sources.title: Catholic Apostolic Exarchate, Burgas parish and publications pages
sources.inspection: The Burgas page's Издания section names a 2005 combined Sluzhebnik, Horologion and prayer book. The exarchate publications page https://www.kae-bg.org/?act=content&rec=136 names a 544-page Holy Week and Resurrection service collection of 2007.
sources.limitations: The listings give no inspected title or approval leaves, exact source recension, or evidence that the 1942 Roman Vulgata was locally received.

sources.title: Russian Catholic parish of the Descent of the Holy Spirit, library catalogue
sources.inspection: The parish list identifies holdings of Roman Slavonic Chrysostom and Sluzhebnik printings, including a 1983 book labelled Recensione Volgata; the prior Eastern inventory enumerates catalogue entries 1465, 1467, 1487, 1504, 1646, 1900, 1902, 1993 and 2148.
sources.limitations: The library list is neither an act of adoption nor evidence that a particular copy was used at the parish altar.

stages.label: Melkite Book of the Divine Liturgy, two complementary parts
stages.date_label: Part 1 catalogued 2006; part 2 catalogued 2007; synodal approval reported 2001
stages.scope: A Church-approved Eucharistic service-book corpus containing Chrysostom in part 1 and Basil and Presanctified in part 2; the two parts are one book state, not two revisions.
stages.witness_label: Patriarchal book identified by the official Letter and DLI holding record 47966
stages.summary: The patriarchal letter reports definitive synodal agreement in 2001 and publication in 2006; the library distinguishes the 2006 Chrysostom and 2007 Basil/Presanctified parts. The patriarch's later decree requires the approved Liturgy books and withdraws other Liturgy books from use.

evidence.claim: Identifies the approved two-part Eucharistic book and the patriarchal use rule.
Supplies the separate publication years, contents and extents of the complementary parts.

stages.limitations: The 2001 approval is not the date of these physical publications. Neither the Arabic text nor the 1992 experimental book was collated; no exact predecessor, component-level revision or first day of uniform use is asserted.
stages.reception: Patriarch Gregorios III's decree orders use of the approved Liturgy books in the Melkite Church; actual compliance in each eparchy is not measured.

stages.label: Holy See approved Greek Hieratikon bearing a 1950 title
stages.scope: Greek celebrant book with Vespers, Orthros and the Liturgies of Chrysostom, Basil and the Presanctified Gifts.
stages.witness_label: Internet Archive copy of the Roman Greek Hieratikon, original title and approval leaves
stages.summary: An approved Roman Greek celebrant book is attested by its own title and approval leaves. The colophon records that printing was completed at Harissa in March 1952.

evidence.locus: Original PDF pp. 3–4, 343, as inspected in the prior Eastern research
evidence.claim: Original title, approval and colophon identify this edition and distinguish title date from end of printing.

stages.limitations: This is a Roman Greek edition state, not a Greek exarchate or Melkite reception state. The press location at Harissa cannot establish Melkite use. No comparison with the 1925 or other Roman Greek books has been made.
stages.reception: Holy See approval is printed in the book; named territorial implementation has not been verified.

stages.label: 1601 liturgies printing for the Italo-Greek Basilians
stages.scope: Printing expressly for the Italo-Greek Basilian monks following the Grottaferrata Typikon, with the three named Eucharistic liturgies.
stages.witness_label: 1601 Zannettus printing, Latin and Greek title leaves in public object photographs
stages.summary: The original title identifies a particular monastic use and printing audience, allowing a bounded local book state without assigning the edition to later Italo-Albanian eparchies.

evidence.locus: Latin title and second Greek title leaf; object description lines 17–27
evidence.claim: Names the three liturgies, Italo-Greek Basilian audience, Grottaferrata Typikon and 1601 Rome imprint.

stages.limitations: The title's declared audience is not a dated use record for a particular monastery, nor approval or reception in Lungro or Piana. No whole copy or exact predecessor has been inspected; its textual distinctness from 1683 remains unestablished.
stages.reception: The printing itself declares the Grottaferrata monastic use it serves; no broader territorial use is inferred.

gaps.missing: Original Arabic title, approval and body leaves for the 1839–1900 Liturgikons, the 1992 experimental text and both parts of the approved book; component collation and eparchial implementation.
gaps.next_source: Acquire the exact volumes named in the patriarchal letter and DLI record 47966, plus the 1991 and 2001 decrees and local use records. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): An Arabic web search for the 2006 Book of the Divine Liturgy found no public scan or title leaves; OPAC SBN title searches returned nothing.
gaps.consequence: The approved book state is documented, but no predecessor or substantive transition is encoded.

gaps.missing: Identified Greek exarchate or Italo-Albanian celebrant copies and adoption evidence; full collation against earlier Roman Greek books. The separate local-reception dossier now records planned Athens 2026 calendar arrangements and selected Italo-Albanian language/calendar evidence; these do not identify receiving Roman 1950/1952 altar copies.
gaps.next_source: Inspect the Hieratikon and local exarchate or eparchial library inventories, title leaves, permissions and use records; compare bounded prayers and rubrics with the 1925 printing. Retain the distinct local-language and calendar findings in greek-italo-local-reception.json without inferring this Roman book’s adoption. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): The exarchate website search API (Ιερατικόν 1 hit, Ευχολόγιον 0, λειτουργικά βιβλία 3, Τυπικόν 2) and the posts read named no receiving celebrant edition. OPAC SBN holdings of the Rome 1950 Hieratikon (PUV0933582, CSA0064106; Grottaferrata state library among them) are holdings, not reception.
gaps.consequence: The Roman edition cannot be placed as a locally received Greek, Piana or Melkite state.

gaps.missing: Exact Greek altar books, original title/approval leaves and dated local adoption for Lungro and Piana; whole-book comparison of the 1601 and 1683 Grottaferrata printings and local manuscripts. Lungro’s named received Arbëresh book and the 2019/2026 local Ordos now have bounded evidence in greek-italo-local-reception.json; original 1967/1968 book and decree reports remain unresolved. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): Piana now has an exact catalogue lead: the 2006 trilingual Ieratikon co-published by the eparchy (OPAC SBN PAL0225607; translator's bibliography). Its altar role, approval, Greek exemplar and parish use are unestablished.
gaps.next_source: Locate copies and approval leaves in Grottaferrata, Lungro and Piana collections. Lungro's official 2026 account attests occasional Liturgy of Saint James without identifying its celebrant book: https://www.eparchialungro.it/2026/02/26/leparchia-di-lungro-nella-chiesa-italiana/ Inspect original Lungro Arbëresh title/approval leaves and Bollettino 3 (1968), pp. 14–16, while keeping Piana calendar reference books distinct from Eucharistic altar books. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): Inspect the title, approval and contents leaves of the Piana 2006 Ieratikon (copies at Piana's Biblioteca comunale Giuseppe Schirò and two other SBN libraries) and any Piana decree introducing it.
gaps.consequence: Grottaferrata printing cannot be used as a surrogate for either modern eparchy or for the unidentified Saint James book.

gaps.missing: Dated Nyírderzs ownership or use, and identity of the Kriva/Krive church in the reported 1666 note. M–920 lacks its front/title and terminal leaves. The college OPAC has an undated possessor entry naming Fr. István Zolcsák of Nyírderzs for M–920, without saying whether it transcribes a mark in the book or records the parish from which the copy came in 2010, and records the Nyírpazony Greek Catholic parish-office stamp at the catalogue locus 74. táblaoldal of the second 1646 copy (Ant10560); neither is dated. A distinct museum copy supplies a 1646-08-23 edition colophon, not local reception.
gaps.next_source: Inspect original M–920 ownership leaves 102–109 and dated Nyírderzs parish inventories. Eger Uu.III.8 has an undated Habina signature on a 1692 title whose relation to the body is described differently in 1992 and 2015; examine its original colophon and the 1775 estate list. The later 1920/1949 states are handled in hungarian-reception.json. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): Inspect Ant10467 (M–920) fols. 102–109 and the possessor entry, and Ant10560 (catalogue locus 74. táblaoldal), at the Szent Atanáz college; date Fr. István Zolcsák's Nyírderzs incumbency from an eparchial schematism. The same OPAC (subject liturgikon, 106 records read) gives later located church possession: a memorial note, written after 1881, recording that a Przemyśl 1840 Sluzhebnik was offered in 1856 for the use of the Sátoraljaújhely Greek Catholic church (Ant30125), a Mikóháza copy with inserted Hungarian translations (Ant30146), and a Lviv 1780 copy from Abaújszántó with references to Hungarian page numbers (Ant30101). These are deferred origin-review inventory records hungarian-satoraljaujhely-przemysl1840-copies and hungarian-abaujszanto-lviv1780-copies; originals remain uninspected.
gaps.consequence: No early Hungarian reception edge follows from the museum imprint or either owner’s possession; the separate modern dossier provides limited later book states.

gaps.period: Roman Vulgata 1940–1953 through the Bulgarian books of 1985–2007
gaps.missing: Proof of Bulgarian receipt of the Roman Vulgata and title, approval and source leaves of the 1985 Eldarov Sluzhebnik and the official 2005 and 2007 local books.
gaps.next_source: Inspect the 1985 celebrant book rather than its bookseller's contents photographs, and obtain the exarchate-listed 2005 and 2007 volumes and their source statements: https://www.kae-bg.org/?act=content&rec=136 Batch 4 (2026-10-21): OPAC SBN searches for Eldarov returned only his theological and historical works; Sluzhebnik title searches with 1985 returned nothing. No source edition or receipt evidence found.
gaps.consequence: An intended Bulgarian audience for Vulgata and a local publication listing do not identify a shared recension, exact Eucharistic text or local use of the Roman book.

gaps.period: Roman Vulgata 1940–1953 and later Russian Catholic holdings
gaps.missing: Dated acts or parish records connecting a specific Roman Slavonic edition to Russian Catholic celebration, and original leaves resolving the 1953, 1956 and 1983 book identities.
gaps.next_source: Match the parish library's item 1900 and other Roman books to inspected title/approval leaves and documented altar use; keep the textual Vulgata states in the existing Byzantine dossier. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): OPAC SBN title searches for Sluzhebnik with 1953, 1956 and 1983 returned nothing; the Roman Slavonic 1942 and 1952 Liturgikon records found there are holdings, not Russian Catholic use.
gaps.consequence: Library possession cannot create a Russian local-reception stage or a new Vulgata textual revision.
